newsitem.title: USA: Electric Boat says big layoffs coming.
newsitem.headline: Electric Boat says big layoffs coming.

text.p: A spokesman for Electric Boat Corp said Friday the company would announce layoffs of up to 1,500 this year, but gave no timing.
Electric Boat is a unit of General Dynamics Corp.

"We expect significant layoffs this year, but I'm not going to nail it down (as to when)," Electric Boat spokesman Neil Ruenzel told Reuters. "We will probably have about a thousand to 1,500 people coming out of the business over the year."
The shipyard currently employs about 9,500 people in Groton. Jobs have declined steadily since 1991 because orders are falling with the end of the Cold War.
New London Day reported Friday that Electric Boat will announce several hundred layoffs next week in the first round of cutbacks.
Ruenzel had no comment on the report, saying it was the company's policy to notify employees first.

Explaining the need for layoffs, Ruenzel said, "Our workload reduces dramatically when we deliver Seawolf and the last Trident submarine (to the Navy). The Seawolf is finished in April and the last Trident is finished in the July-August timeframe."
Ruenzel also said Electric Boat's plan to team up with Newport News Shipbuilding on building a new class of submarine should be final by the end of this month.
